title: Requirements matrix
description: requirements_matrix inside the case manifest.json [simulation-workflow.en.md 1, 13.1]. A candidate is complete only when every row is pass [simulation-workflow.en.md 13.3]. Row fields follow 13.1 and the case outputs; fields marked 'plugin' are added so the gate can tell measured and current evidence from stale or unmeasured claims. Other manifest keys are allowed.

id.description: Story rows reuse the beat id.

covers.description: (plugin) Ids of the contract.story.beats this row verifies. Without covers, a row covers the beat whose id equals the row id, if one exists; a row may cover several beats and a beat may be covered by several rows. The gate fails when a beat has no covering row or covers names a beat that does not exist [paper A.1.1 Specification audit: missing requirements remain unverified; paper A.2: matrix rows cover the spec's requirements; simulation-workflow.en.md 1.2 empty missing_beats, 13.1].

pass_predicate.description: Pass threshold [13.1], for people. The numbers it uses are stated again in tolerances and measures, which bin/spec_audit.py checks.

tolerances.description: (plugin) Every distance, penetration, position or error tolerance the predicate uses, with where it comes from [bin/spec_audit.py tolerance_basis].

measures.description: (plugin) Other measured quantities the predicate compares (speeds, counts, fractions, lower bounds on distance). A row needs at least one tolerance or measure: a judgement nobody can measure is not a row [bin/spec_audit.py measurable].

status.description: pass/fail/unknown/blocked [skill.md:47; simulation-workflow.en.md:87,425]. stale (plugin): the row was measured, but an input it was measured on has changed, so it must be re-run [paper A.2.2 Feedback and acceptance, selective invalidation].

reason.description: Why the row has its current status.

verified_by.description: (plugin) Script that measured the status. A pass with no measuring script is not evidence [skill.md 'A successful Blender operator is not evidence'].

input_hashes.description: (plugin) SHA-256 of each input the evidence was measured on (candidate .blend, cache, manifest, and the verifier script itself), keyed by path. A mismatch makes the row stale.

tolerance.description: One tolerance and its basis. Default rule: value_m = max(screen_m, solver_m), where screen_m is 5 pixels at the reference resolution at that distance (worldagent_measure.scale.pixel_footprint) and solver_m is the solver's resolution (collision margin for rigid bodies, one grid cell for grid solvers, collision distance for cloth and soft body). The reference resolution is the final render resolution scaled up, aspect ratio kept, until its longer side is at least 1920 px (a 320x180 final render uses 1920x1080; 3840x2160 is used as is), so a low test resolution does not loosen tolerances. A smaller value only when the request asks for that precision (basis request). Numeric tolerances (centre of mass, volume) are a ratio of the object's size, not an absolute length. Basis outcome: a threshold derived from an outcome the request states (e.g. 'the tower falls over' -> top block centre below 0.45 of its start height); derivation names the request clause. An outcome may be looser than the default rule, never tighter: an outcome value_m also gives screen_m and solver_m and is at least max(screen_m, solver_m); a tighter value needs basis request. A ratio outcome is not checked against the default rule.

quantity.description: What is measured, e.g. 'penetration depth crate_a vs floor'.

value_m.description: Tolerance as a length in metres.

ratio.description: Tolerance as a fraction of the length named in of.

of.description: The length a ratio refers to, e.g. 'crate_a bbox diagonal'.

screen_m.description: 5 pixels at the reference resolution (the final resolution scaled up to a longer side of at least 1920 px) at that distance, in metres.

derivation.description: The calculation, e.g. '5 px at 1920x1080 from the camera at 1.6 m = 3.0 mm' or 'Bullet collision margin 1 mm', or the request clause for basis request or outcome.

measure.description: One measured quantity and its comparison, e.g. {quantity: 'crate speed, last second', comparison: '<', value: 0.05, unit: 'm/s'}. An upper bound or equality on a length belongs in tolerances.
